title: Property tax — rules, rates and assessment history

sections.title: 1. Governing rules (verified)
sections.intro: These are the rules that decide what Property A costs after it transfers. They are the single largest controllable cost in the decision.

rows.note: Art. XIII A caps the general levy at 1%; counties add voter-approved debt on top.

rows.item: Maximum annual increase in assessed value while ownership is unchanged
rows.note: This is why the assessed value of Property A ($550,540) is ~18% of market value.

rows.item: Santa Clara County average ad valorem rate (all cities)
rows.note: 1% base plus voter-approved debt. Actual rate depends on the parcel's tax rate area (TRA).

rows.item: Cupertino city average ad valorem rate
rows.note: City average reported from the Assessor's 2025-26 report; the exact TRA rate is printed on the tax bill and was not available (no APN). Flagged F-03.

rows.item: San Francisco secured property tax rate, FY2026-27
rows.note: Prior year (FY2025-26) was 1.18268325%.
One-time BOE-266 filing with the county assessor; file by February 15 for the full year.

rows.value: 2 installments: Nov 1 (delinquent Dec 10) and Feb 1 (delinquent Apr 10)
rows.note: 10% penalty on the delinquent installment, then 1.5%/month and eventual tax-default after June 30.
Form BOE-305-AH with the Clerk of the Board; a county-specific fee applies. Confirm on the county site — flagged F-09.

rows.item: Documentary transfer tax on a sale (Santa Clara County + Cupertino)
rows.note: County charges $0.55/$500 and credits a conforming city tax at the same rate against it, so the combined rate stays $1.10/$1,000.

rows.item: Documentary transfer tax on an inheritance transfer
rows.value: Generally no tax on a transfer for no consideration
rows.note: The tax is measured by consideration; a trustee's deed distributing property to a beneficiary ordinarily carries no consideration. Confirm with the title company/escrow — left blank, flagged F-10.

sections.title: 2. Proposition 19 — the inheritance tax that is not called a tax
sections.intro: California has no inheritance tax, but it does have a reassessment on death. For Property A the difference between keeping and losing the parent-child exclusion is roughly $21,000/year at the expected transfer date.

rows.value: Parent→child exclusion applies only to the parent's principal residence that becomes the child's principal residence within 1 year
rows.note: RTC 63.2(a)(1)(A). Rental or second-home use does not qualify — the exclusion is lost entirely.
RTC 63.2(a)(1)(B). File BOE-266 with the Santa Clara County Assessor.

rows.value: BOE-19-P — within 3 years of the transfer, or before sale to a third party
rows.note: Miss the 3-year window and the exclusion can only be applied prospectively.

rows.value: Factored base year value + indexed amount
rows.note: Anything above the limit is added to the base year value. The limit is set against the appraised market value on the transfer date.
Adjusted every two years using the FHFA California house price index. $1,022,600 for 2023–2025; $1,000,000 for 2021–2023.
BOE publishes the next figure before it applies. Left blank — do not assume a figure. Flagged F-04.

rows.item: Formula when market value exceeds the limit
rows.value: New base = market value − indexed amount (equivalently: old base + excess above the limit)
rows.note: BOE worked example: base $300,000, market $1,500,000, limit $1,300,000 → new base $500,000.

rows.value: The exclusion is removed as of the date eligibility for the homeowners' exemption ends
rows.note: RTC 63.2(a)(1)(C): the full base year value is enrolled the following lien date. 'Move in for a year, then rent it' does not preserve the benefit.

rows.item: Trust-held property — date of change in ownership
rows.value: Date the revocable trust becomes irrevocable (normally the date of death)
rows.note: BOE FAQ #9 and RTC 61(h). The trust gets no special treatment under Prop 19.

sections.title: 5. Rate reconciliation — where the supplied numbers disagree with published rates
sections.intro: Each line either reconciles or is flagged. Rates are official; the supplied taxes are not.

rows.note: Arithmetic on supplied bills. Sits between the county average (1.19%) and a rate that includes fixed direct assessments and parcel taxes.
$7,210 − (1.193% × $539,740) = $770. Fixed assessments are levied per parcel and do not grow with value. Assumption A26.
Within 2% of the 2025 bill, consistent with the 2% assessment cap.

rows.note: $2,440 ÷ 1.18268325%. The supplied assessment of $114,250 is roughly half of this — most likely land-only. Flagged F-05; use the tax amount, not the assessment column, for modelling.
